newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks weaken in active Thursday trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks weaken in active Thursday trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean stocks slipped on Thursday as investors siphoned off funds into an issue by a local merchant bank but brokers said they expected the market to recoup its losses as soon as the issue was out of the way.
The main industrial index shed 44.04 points to close at 10,208.82.

"Funds have been siphoned off into the NMB issue but we are expecting the market to strengthen a bit post-the NMB issue as people assess their portfolios and see where they can put their money," one broker said.
Brokers said the issue by NMB (National Merchant Bank) -- which closed at midday -- looked oversubscribed.
The bank, owned by black Zimbabwean businessmen, makes its debut on the Zimbabwean Stock Exchange on Thursday. It will also be listed in London.

On the local bourse on Thursday, bankers Barclays and agriculture investor Chemco each dropped 100 cents to 3,200 and 4,400 respectively while agricultural products manufacturer Acacia at 350, clothing retailers Edgars at 775 and Truworths at 900 all shed 25 cents.
Winery Afdis, glass firm PGI and clothing and furniture retailer Tedco each lost 20 cents to 460, 630 and 250 respectively.
A handful of counters bucked the trend, notably merchant banker FMB FMB.ZI which rose 100 cents to 4,500 as did publisher Zimpapers to 5,000.
The mining board saw limited trading with Wankie Colliery adding 15 cents to 525. The secondary mining index put on 5.46 points to end at 979.17.
